Subject: Proposed SIEM-proxy pattern for AcmeHealth private deployment

Hi Sofia,

Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday. AcmeHealth security wants to avoid direct internet egress from their VPC for logs/metrics/traces but still needs us to receive telemetry for support and analytics. Scanline put together a short proposal for a SIEM-proxy that sits in the customer VPC and forwards to a hardened endpoint.

Key asks from Acme:
- Support for Splunk HEC and Syslog (CEF) sinks
- Mutual TLS from the proxy to our endpoint; certs issued per-customer
- Ability to buffer on disk when network intermittent (max 48h)
- Proof points for data minimization (PII scrubbing) and audit trails

I attached a quick diagram and the SOC2 questionnaire they started filling out. Can you confirm whether Redwood Private supports this proxy topology and if there are any gotchas?

Attachments: scanline-proxy-arch.png, acme-soc2-questionnaire.pdf

Thanks,
Alex Reed
Scanline Security

On Wed, Mar 14, 2028 at 09:12 AM Alex Reed <alex@scanline-sec.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for the quick sync yesterday...

Alex — thanks for the diagram and the questionnaire. We can support the general pattern you outlined, with a few recommended controls and constraints to keep the data plane predictable and compliant. High level:

- Topology we prefer: lightweight local forwarder (Vector/Fluentd/Filebeat) -> customer-side SIEM-proxy (container/EC2) -> mTLS to Redwood Private ingress. The SIEM-proxy performs batching, schema normalization, and optional PII redaction before egress.
- Auth: per-customer mTLS with short-lived certs; control plane issues and rotates certs via our API.
- Buffering: support for local disk buffering with configurable retention (we recommend <= 72 hours at default, review with compliance).
- Protocols: Splunk HEC, OTLP/HTTP for traces/metrics, Syslog/CEF for legacy logs.
- Observability hooks: the proxy should export health metrics (OTLP/prom) and tracing spans to your local collector so we can correlate errors without receiving full payloads.

Open questions for you that will change the config:
1) Which log classes must be forwarded (app logs, audit logs, access logs)?
2) Required retention for buffered copy on the proxy (default suggestion: 48-72h).
3) Are there in-line PII redaction rules they want applied at the proxy or upstream in Redwood?

Next steps: I’ll loop in our infra owner for the proxy runtime details and a short runbook. Can we do a 30-min call tomorrow to lock retention and cert rotation cadence?

Cc: Naomi — please see the bullet list below; particularly want your SOC2 mapping for the retention and audit requirements. I attached a sample proxy config and a quick architecture diagram for reference.

Attachments: siem-proxy-example.conf, scanline-proxy-arch.png

Best,

- Default buffer retention we should propose to customers (48 vs 72 hours)

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 15 Mar 2028 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Proposed SIEM-proxy pattern for AcmeHealth private deployment

Thanks for the ping — short technical notes and recommended defaults from runtime/infra perspective: 

- Supported collectors: Vector is our preferred default for customers (lightweight, OTLP first-class). We also document Filebeat and Fluentd templates.
- Protocols: OTLP/HTTP (gzip) for metrics/traces; Splunk HEC over TLS and Syslog (TCP+TLS) for logs.
- Sidecar vs Daemonset: recommend daemonset/host-logging for infra logs and sidecar for app-specific logs where volume is small.
- Buffering: enable disk-backed buffers with a default cap of 50GB or 72 hours, whichever comes first. Configurable by customer; warn that larger buffers increase RTO during restore.
- Backpressure: proxy must implement bounded queues + LRU disk spool; when queue is full, drop non-critical debug logs first and emit a backpressure metric. We expose these metrics to Redwood via an OTLP health span so that we can trigger fallback policies.
- Auth and certs: mTLS with per-customer identity. Control plane will issue a CSR endpoint. Rotation cadence default: 30 days; can be shortened for higher-compliance customers. Revocation via short CRL window + serial revocation on our API.
- Data minimization: recommend allowing the proxy to apply simple regex redaction for PII fields and a configurable allowlist of JSON keys to forward. Complex tokenization should happen upstream before logs hit the proxy.

I attached a small example config (siem-proxy-example.conf) we can share with the customer. If Naomi signs off on the SOC2 mapping to these defaults I’m comfortable shipping the guidance.

— Vivek
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>
To: Alex Reed <alex@scanline-sec.com>, Mike Thompson <mike@acmehealth.com>

Date: Fri, 16 Mar 2028 16:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed SIEM-proxy pattern for AcmeHealth private deployment

Alex / Mike — thanks for the diagram and patience. From a compliance perspective the proposed pattern is acceptable with the following items to confirm before we finalize: 

1) Retention: default buffer retention set to 72 hours; Acme must confirm any retention beyond that or we will require a signed exception.
2) PII redaction: we can support configurable regex-based scrubbing in the proxy; for sensitive PHI fields we recommend upstream tokenization prior to forwarding.
3) Audit trail: the proxy should log certificate issuance/revocation events to a local audit log; control plane will ingest metadata (no raw payload).
4) Proof: we will provide an evidence packet (configuration snapshot, cert lifecycle logs, and policy mapping) for the SOC2 review.

Action items:
- Acme to confirm log classes and any retention exceptions by EOD Mon 2028-03-20.
- Scanline to deploy the sample proxy in a dev VPC and share metrics/health spans.
- Redwood to provide cert CSR endpoint and the sample config (attached).

If we get those confirmations we can produce a short runbook and a minimal attestation package for their auditors.

Regards,
Naomi Feldman
Security & Compliance, Redwood Inference
